summary: Automate provisioning of model-runbook Slack channels with gated access and Confluence linkage
description:
Issue summary:
We want a self-service automation that creates Slack channels for model runbooks (per-model and per-team), wires up a Confluence runbook page template, sets appropriate channel metadata, and enforces gated access and lifecycle policy.

Background / rationale:
Runtime Ops and Platform SRE teams repeatedly create ad-hoc runbook channels for new model rollouts. Current manual process results in inconsistent naming, missing runbook pages, and overly broad membership. This slows onboarding for oncall and increases blast radius during incidents.

Impact:
- Slow response during incidents when runbook channel or page is missing.
- Security: channels often include broader groups than needed.
- Operational toil for Platform and SRE to create and configure channels.

Requirements (high level):
1) Self-service form (via internal Slack command or Jira request) to provision a runbook channel with parameters: model-name, owning-team, sensitivity-level (public/limited/strict), initial members (team alias or list), and optional reviewers.
2) Automation creates Slack channel with canonical name: ops-runbook-<model-short>-<team> and sets channel purpose and topic with metadata (model version pinned, contact alias).
3) Automation creates Confluence runbook page from template and posts the page link into channel. Page should include sections for incident steps, fallback models, contact list, playbook steps.
4) Access control: for sensitivity-level limited/strict, channel membership must be gated via an approval flow (approver for owning team + Security). For strict, membership should be limited to explicit lists (no @org-wide roles).
5) Lifecycle policy: channel auto-archives after 90 days of inactivity; owners get automated reminders at 30/60/80 days.
6) Audit logging: create Jira ticket and log create/update events in an audit Confluence index and in platform audit logs.
7) RBAC integration: provisioning must respect existing Okta groups and map aliases into channel membership.

Acceptance criteria:
- A developer can request a channel via /create-runbook with the required fields and see a confirmation message.
- Channel is created within 10 minutes, with Confluence page linked and a stub runbook present.
- For "limited"/"strict" levels, the approval workflow triggers and membership is not granted until approval is recorded.
- Audit entry appears in the central runbooks Confluence index and in the audit log.

Security considerations:
- Strict-level channels must not include service accounts with broad permissions unless explicitly approved.
- Confluence pages generated should inherit space ACLs consistent with the owning team's policy; do not make pages public by default.

Operational notes / constraints:
- We should reuse existing Slack provisioning bot and Confluence templates rather than creating new infra.
- Work with Identity to map aliases and ensure Okta group refresh is available in the approval window.

Suggested rollout plan:
1) Implement automation in staging and test with platform-sre pod.
2) Pilot with two active model teams (recommend runtime-ops and search-models).
3) After pilot, open to wider teams and document process in internal docs.

Related links / references:
- Confluence runbook template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNBOOKS/Model-Runbook-Template
- Slack provisioning bot repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools-slack-provisioner
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - request-oriented task. Current manual steps: 1) Create channel in Slack 2) Manually add members 3) Create Confluence page from template and paste link 4) Notify oncall. We want to replace these with an automated flow.
investigation_notes:
Spoke with runtime-ops (Mar 9). They reported 7 ad-hoc runbook channels created in last 60 days; 3 lacked Confluence pages. Identity confirmed Okta group API supports on-demand membership queries but rate limits may apply. Slack provisioning bot can create channels and set topics; it currently lacks an approval hook. Confluence templates exist in RUNBOOKS space; template automation will require a service account with create-page permission scoped to RUNBOOKS.
Potential blockers: Okta rate limits for group expansion, approval flow UX in Slack, and strict-level membership enforcement requiring an additional step with Identity team.
